body.text: Why is Bodrum's Museum of Underwater Archaeology world-class (Uluburun shipwreck)?

Built between 1406 and 1523 by the Knights of St. John, Bodrum Castle holds the world's premier maritime archaeology collection, recognized with a Special Commendation in the 1995 European Museum of the Year Awards. Its centerpiece is the Late Bronze Age Uluburun shipwreck—carrying copper ingots, cobalt glass, ivory, and Queen Nefertiti's gold scarab.

Excavated off Kaş, the Uluburun cargo preserves an intact snapshot of 14th-century BCE Mediterranean diplomacy and trade, displayed inside a full-scale hull reconstruction. Beyond the Uluburun hall, [Bodrum Sualtı Arkeoloji Müzesi](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=MRK&SectionId=BSA01) spans five national castle towers—including the 47.5-meter French Tower—plus amphora courtyards and the separate Serçe Limanı 11th-century Glass Wreck Hall.
What are the 2026 ticket prices and hours?

In 2026, foreign visitors pay €20 for Bodrum Castle and the Museum of Underwater Archaeology (covered by MuseumPass Aegean at €95 and MuseumPass Türkiye at €165), plus €6 extra for the Serçe Limanı Glass Wreck Hall. The castle opens daily at 08:30, closing at 17:30 in winter and up to 21:00–22:00 in peak summer.

Verify current hours and e-tickets via [Turkish Museums](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/2168-mugla-bodrum-underwater-archaeology-museum/2168/4) or the [muze.gov.tr e-ticket catalog](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-ekle?catalogNo=WEB-ZPO01-87-009). During summer night-museum season (1 June to 1 October), evening sessions run 19:00–22:00 ([Bodrum Castle 2026 Guide](https://bodrumguru.com/en/bodrum-museum-of-underwater-archaeology/)). Note that the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus is closed on Mondays.
What remains of the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus?

Set ten minutes uphill from Bodrum's bazaar in Tepecik, the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus—one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World—survives mainly as an excavated rectangular foundation pit, subterranean drainage tunnels, and scattered marble column drums. A small on-site pavilion displays scale reconstructions explaining how King Mausolus's 45-meter tomb once stood.

Earthquakes toppled the 4th-century BCE monument, and the Knights of St. John later quarried its green volcanic stone and marble blocks directly into Bodrum Castle's walls, while British excavators moved key frieze slabs to London in the 1850s ([Mausoleum at Halicarnassus 2026 Guide](https://departly.co.uk/to/turkey/mausoleum-at-halicarnassus/)). At €3, it pairs naturally with the castle ([Bodrum Museums 2026](https://bodrumguru.com/en/museums-and-places-to-visit-in-bodrum/)).
How do you walk from the castle to Bardakçı windmills?

Leave Bodrum Castle's main gate, walk west along the waterfront promenade past Bodrum Marina, and follow the paved uphill road climbing the ridge between Bodrum Bay and Gümbet/Bardakçı Bay. The route covers roughly 1.6 km and takes 20 to 25 minutes on foot, opening onto twin-bay views at the 18th-century stone windmills.

The final stretch is steep but paved throughout ([Bodrum Windmills Route Guide](https://www.advantour.com/turkey/bodrum/windmills.htm)). Plan your climb for the final hour before sunset when the castle walls glow across the harbor ([Bodrum Windmills Guide](https://bodrumguru.com/en/bodrum-windmills/)), and take a short taxi back down if you stay past dusk.
Use this quick Bodrum heritage checklist:

items: Schedule the Mausoleum Tuesday through Sunday—avoid Monday when its gate is shut.
Wear grippy flat shoes for Bodrum Castle's polished stone stairs and cobbles.
Carry water for the uphill ridge walk to the Bardakçı windmills.
Add the €6 Glass Wreck Hall if maritime trade history interests you.

faq.q: How much time do you need inside Bodrum Castle?
faq.a: Plan two to two-and-a-half hours to tour the Uluburun Shipwreck Hall, the towers, the amphora gardens, and the rampart viewpoints without rushing.

faq.q: Is Bodrum Castle open on Mondays in 2026?
faq.a: Yes. Bodrum Castle and the Museum of Underwater Archaeology are open seven days a week, whereas the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus and the Zeki Müren Arts Museum close on Mondays.

faq.q: Can you walk between Bodrum Castle and the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus?
faq.a: Yes. The Mausoleum sits about 700 meters northwest of the castle in Tepecik—roughly a 10-minute walk uphill from the marina and bazaar.

faq.q: Are the Bodrum windmills safe to walk down after sunset?
faq.a: The upper ridge path is dimly lit and uneven in spots after dark, so taking a short taxi back to Bodrum center is the safest option once twilight fades.

faq.q: Can you use a dolmuş to reach the Bardakçı windmills?
faq.a: Yes. Take the Bardakçı dolmuş from Bodrum bus station and ask the driver for the windmills; it drops you on the main road about 400 to 500 meters below the ridge.

faq.q: Are Bodrum Castle ticket prices scheduled to change after 2026?
faq.a: Published Ministry guidance indicates foreign-visitor tariffs are scheduled to rise from €20 to €22 for Bodrum Castle and from €3 to €5 for the Mausoleum starting 1 April 2027.
